title: Constant module realization and terminal sections on a slice
statement: Let C be a small category, T a Grothendieck topology, A a commutative ring in the same coefficient universe, and U an object. Restrict the constant-ring sheafification unit from T to T/U. Construct L_A by sheafifying constant module presheaves along this unit, and S_A by forgetting and restricting scalars along the unit and evaluating at the terminal object. Construct the adjunction L_A left adjoint S_A. Construct natural isomorphisms identifying L_A with restriction to U of global constant module realization and identifying L_A followed by S_A with ordinary sections of the constant sheaf of A-modules. Also construct the natural isomorphism commuting ordinary scalar change with slice restriction. Finally, for arbitrary adjunctions F_0 left adjoint R_0, F_1 left adjoint R_1 and a natural isomorphism theta:F_1 C_0 isomorphic F_0, define the mate kappa:R_1 to C_0 R_0 of theta inverse and prove eta_0(M)=eta_1(M) followed by kappa(F_1(M)) and R_0(theta(M)). All constructions use sheafification universal properties and proved comparison maps [def-sfb-site-derived-constant-module-functor, lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence].

proof.text: The constant module presheaf is left adjoint to evaluation at the terminal slice object: the unit is identity and the counit consists of restriction maps along the unique maps to the terminal object. Compose with module sheafification to construct localAdjunction.

Restrict the global module sheafification unit to the slice and transpose by slice module sheafification. Its underlying additive map and both sheafification units are locally bijective, so the comparison is invertible. Transpose naturality by the same Hom equivalence. Forgetting variable scalars gives a sheaf of A-modules; sheafify its constant generators to construct fixedConstantIso and then sectionsIso.

Bundle the existing proved scalar-change/slice isomorphisms and their naturality from AdicPerfectModelCompleteReduction as a natural isomorphism. The choice is from a proved Nonempty theorem, without any new unproved data.

For arbitrary adjunctions F_0 left adjoint R_0 and F_1 left adjoint R_1 and theta:F_1 C isomorphic F_0, define the mate on N by eta_0(R_1 N) followed by R_0 of theta inverse followed by C of epsilon_1(N). Naturality follows from naturality of eta_0, theta and epsilon_1. For the unit equation, move eta_1 through eta_0 by unit naturality, move it through theta inverse by theta naturality, and cancel F_1(eta_1) followed by epsilon_1 using the left triangle identity. The final theta inverse followed by theta cancels.
